children.title: Revised: Computational Creativity and Autonomous Problem Formulation

detail.title: Revised: Computational Creativity and Autonomous Problem Formulation
detail.summary: Autonomous problem formulation frameworks are significantly enhanced by the capacity for agents to learn value systems directly from observations, shifting problem identification from static heuristics to adaptive, learned evaluation models.
detail.reason: Revising to integrate findings on automated value system learning as a critical component of problem formulation.

children.title: Revised: Mechanisms of Unassigned Objective Discovery

detail.title: Revised: Mechanisms of Unassigned Objective Discovery
detail.summary: Objective discovery in autonomous systems is mediated by the interplay between learned value systems and cognitive effort, allowing for goal generation that emerges from interaction dynamics rather than explicit assignment.
detail.reason: Revising to integrate findings on cognitive effort and value system learning.

detail.title: Mechanisms of Unprompted Complexity
detail.summary: Complexity in autonomous agents arises from the recursive loop between problem formulation, knowledge manipulation, and the automatic learning of value systems, which continuously redefines the agent's environment and internal models.
detail.reason: Fulfilling synthesis requirements for the active project.

detail.statement: Computational creativity frameworks require robust integration between formulation, representation, and adaptive learning of value systems to support autonomous progress.
detail.reason: Updated to reflect that value system learning is a critical, missing integration point in many baseline creativity models.

detail.statement: Computational creativity frameworks depend on structured decomposition of problem-solving components to allow for independent modular improvement of formulation and evaluation.
detail.reason: Reinforced by evidence that automated value system learning can be treated as a specific module within a broader decomposition.

detail.statement: Computational creativity frameworks require robust integration between formulation and value system learning, now increasingly supported by shared query understanding in multi-agent environments.
detail.reason: New evidence confirms the necessity of shared query understanding in open multi-agent systems for successful creativity integration.

detail.statement: Computational creativity frameworks depend on structured decomposition of problems, which can be significantly enhanced by Agreement Technologies in open systems.
detail.reason: Agreement Technologies provide the formal structure required for collaborative, decomposed problem-solving in open environments.
